properties.digitized_from: Potrero Power Station Design for Development, final (February 26, 2020), Figure 6.2.3 - Building Height Plan (printed p.245, PDF p.247).
properties.digitization_method: Traced from the Potrero Power Station Design for Development's own Figure 6.2.3 (Building Height Plan, p.245) -- an adopted regulatory diagram with a printed scale bar, north arrow, and real street labels (Illinois St, Georgia St, Louisiana St, Maryland St, Delaware St, 22nd St, Humboldt St, 23rd St), not an illustrative rendering. Georeferenced using 9 real street-intersection control points fetched from OpenStreetMap via this project's own src/fetch_streets.py, fit as a least-squares affine transform (the same transform used for this site's other blocks -- see e.g. Block 11's entry for the full discussion of why real-building anchors were tried and discarded for this particular site). Residual error against the fitted control points is roughly 8-24m. ADDED 2026-09-14: this block was accidentally omitted from the initial pass through Figure 6.2.3 -- Blocks 1, 3, 4, 5, 9, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, and the remainder of Block 7 were traced and added, but Block 8 (positioned between them, south of Humboldt St) was skipped by oversight. Traced polygon additionally clipped against the real, confirmed Sophie Maxwell and UCSF Block 2 parcels and Prequel Park's approximate geometry, per this project's standard practice. CORRECTED 2026-09-16: user-flagged pattern of blocks encroaching on real streets across the site (Block 3, Block 11, Block 12) led to rebuilding this whole block layer from scratch using proper GCP-based georeferencing (GDAL's gdaltransform with a thin-plate-spline transform, the same technique QGIS's Georeferencer uses) instead of patching individual curbs. Installed GDAL, computed 8 real street-intersection ground control points from OpenStreetMap data (Craig Lane x Maryland St, 22nd St x Maryland/Louisiana St, Humboldt St x Maryland/Delaware/Georgia Lane, 23rd St x Maryland/Georgia Lane), precisely located each in the source diagram (Figure 6.2.3) via programmatic black-pixel border detection cross-checked with visual ruler crops, and fit a TPS transform. Re-traced this block's own corner pixels the same way and ran them through the new transform. This corrected transform disagrees with the original 9-point affine transform by tens of meters in places -- e.g. it revealed the original trace had Blocks 3/4 shifted east into the excavation pit/street area, and Blocks 11/12 roughly 2x too deep -- and the new positions now land within real, distinct site features (buildings, graded lots) visible in satellite imagery rather than straddling roads. Known residual limitation: GCP street positions are centerline-based (matching OSM convention), while a block boundary should sit at the near curb, so any edge close to a GCP street can land a few meters into that street after transformation -- checked for and corrected on this block's street-facing edge(s) where applicable using this project's already-established grid bearing (356.5 deg) and, where available, an independently diagram-measured depth/width. Treat corrected vertex positions as accurate to roughly 10-15m (tighter than the original 8-24m transform, but still not survey-grade). RE-CORRECTED 2026-09-16 (same day, third pass): the independent per-block TPS re-trace (see above) still measured each block's own 4 corners in isolation, which -- despite using the same transform -- left small (3-12m) spurious gaps or misalignments at boundaries the diagram actually draws as shared or tightly-spaced between adjacent blocks (caught after the user pointed out the diagram itself has ~zero wasted space and specifically that the PG&E switchyard polygon sits directly against Block 5 in the diagram, not ~60m away as this dataset had it). Re-measured EVERY block's corners in a single consistent pass using programmatic black-pixel border detection (long contiguous runs = real borders, filtered from text/dimension-arrow strokes by requiring the run to span nearly the full block height/width), cross-validated with fine-pixel-gridline crops, so that shared or consistently-measured boundaries between neighboring blocks now come from the same underlying pixel measurements rather than independent eyeball estimates. Batch-transformed through the same GDAL/TPS fit as before. This pass also corrected several block extents that were measured imprecisely in the prior pass (e.g. Block 5's real stepped/notched south edge, Block 11's true position -- it does NOT sit flush against Block 15, there is real Power Station Park open space between them). GCP CORRECTION 2026-09-16 (fourth pass): user flagged that Block 8/12 should touch Delaware Street with park space between them, and that Block 3/4's shapes looked off -- investigation found the root cause was a single mis-measured ground control point. The 'Delaware St x Humboldt St' GCP used for the whole site's TPS transform had been placed at pixel (2227, 986), which is actually deep inside Building 9's own footprint in the diagram, not on Delaware Street at all -- confirmed by comparing pixel spacing between the three Humboldt-row GCPs (Maryland/Delaware/Georgia Lane): Maryland-to-Georgia-Lane's pixel:real-world ratio implied Delaware should sit at roughly pixel x=2020, not 2227, and a direct color-transition scan at y=986 confirmed the real street gap is at x=1994-2035. Corrected the GCP to (2015, 986) (same real-world coordinate, just the right pixel) and re-ran the TPS transform for the whole site. This produced large corrections concentrated exactly where the user's complaint pointed -- Block 4 shifted 33-60m, Block 3's east corners ~28-33m, Block 8's east corners ~29-31m, Block 12's east corners ~26-27m -- while blocks far from the error (5, 15, 7, 11, PG&E) shifted well under 5m, consistent with a localized GCP error rather than a global transform problem. 2026-09-29 accuracy audit: the source URL cited for this file (the August 22, 2019 public-review draft #2 of the D4D at default.sfplanning.org) is dead (404); the text above describes the final D4D (dated February 26, 2020), so source_doc_urls now points to potreropower_D4D_final.pdf, where Figure 6.2.3 Building Height Plan is on printed p.245 (PDF p.247) with a scale bar (0-400 ft), a north arrow and the street labels listed above. In the final D4D's Figure 6.2.3 the green strip between Block 15 and Block 11 is labelled 'LOUISIANA PASEO'; 'POWER STATION PARK' is labelled north of Block 11, between it and Block 7 (so the statement above that Power Station Park lies between Blocks 15 and 11 is corrected). The regulatory_context statements on heights, units and construction status were corrected on the same date; the committed geometry was not changed. 2026-10-02: public-text pass. accuracy_caveat, notes reworded for readers (meaning unchanged; no change to the shape, status, use or geometry_type); previous wording -- accuracy_caveat: 'APPROXIMATE -- this block is not yet built (not started as of the 2024 annual compliance report, March 2025; construction expected to begin in fall 2026 per the Chronicle of Aug 3, 2026) and this file has not matched it to an Assessor parcel. DataSF Parcels (checked 2026-09-29) lists an active lot, 4232022 at 151 Humboldt St (recorded 2022-08-30), which is the address the Chronicle gives for the Block 8 building and which lies almost entirely within this approximate footprint; the Block 8 design-review memo itself lists the parent lots 4175/017, 4175/002, 4232/001 and 4232/006. Whether this polygon should be replaced by lot 4232022 is undecided (owner decision). Traced from an adopted regulatory diagram via multi-point real-street georeferencing (see digitization_method), but this diagram is dated Feb 2020 and may not reflect later design changes (as already found for the adjacent UCSF/Sophie Maxwell area). Treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 10-25m, not survey-grade. Rebuilt 2026-09-16 via GDAL GCP/TPS georeferencing -- see digitization_method. Re-measured 2026-09-16 (third pass) in a single consistent pixel-detection pass across the whole block layout -- see digitization_method. Re-corrected 2026-09-16 (fourth pass) after fixing a mis-measured GCP -- see digitization_method.'; notes: 'Approximate polygon for a real, D4D-adopted block (final D4D, Feb 26, 2020: Table 3.1.1 and Figure 6.2.3) -- see accuracy_caveat. properties.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- this block is not yet built (not started as of the 2024 annual compliance report, March 2025; construction expected to begin in fall 2026 per the Chronicle of Aug 3, 2026) and this record has not matched it to an Assessor parcel. DataSF Parcels (checked 2026-09-29) lists an active lot, 4232022 at 151 Humboldt St (recorded 2022-08-30), which is the address the Chronicle gives for the Block 8 building and which lies almost entirely within this approximate footprint; the Block 8 design-review memo itself lists the parent lots 4175/017, 4175/002, 4232/001 and 4232/006. Whether this polygon should be replaced by lot 4232022 is undecided (a decision for Pier & Point). Traced from an adopted regulatory diagram, fitted to real street positions at multiple points, but this diagram is dated Feb 2020 and may not reflect later design changes (as already found for the adjacent UCSF/Sophie Maxwell area). Treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 10-25m, not survey-grade. The shape was rebuilt on 2026-09-16 with a more careful fit of the diagram to the map, re-measured the same day consistently across the whole block layout, and corrected again that day after one mis-measured reference point was fixed. How this shape was traced, including earlier versions, is logged in its data file in the public data repository (https://github.com/pierandpoint/record).
properties.why_no_real_parcel: A real Assessor parcel may exist under this block (part of the site's larger, largely unaddressed footprint), but it has not been subdivided per the masterplan's individual named blocks -- this uses hand-traced approximate geometry instead. DataSF Parcels (checked 2026-09-29) lists an active lot, 4232022 (151 Humboldt St, recorded 2022-08-30), that lies almost entirely within this footprint; the Block 8 design-review memo lists four parent lots (4175/017, 4175/002, 4232/001, 4232/006), so the block spanned several real lots before the 2022 subdivision.
properties.regulatory_context: Figure 6.2.3 of the final D4D shows Block 8 with two height limits by its colour-coded labels: 125 ft (along Humboldt and Maryland Streets) and 85 ft (its south-east part); the two '90'MAX' labels are tick-ended dimension lines, not heights (the design-review staff memo describes D4D standard A.8.1 as letting the part of the building above the streetwall extend up to 90 feet in depth from the Humboldt Street and Maryland Street property lines). The D4D's Permitted Uses table (Table 3.1.1) confirms residential is permitted here (Laboratory and Life Science are not). Foster + Partners is the design architect per the March 2022 design-review approval and the Chronicle (Aug 3, 2026). Unit counts differ by source: 249 (SF YIMBY, March 2021), 339 (2022 design-review approval), 342 (Chronicle, Aug 2026). The approved height is about 125 ft to the last occupied floor plus up to 20 ft of screened mechanical (plan set); SF YIMBY reported 140 ft (March 2021) and 156 ft (March 2022). Construction had not started as of the 2024 annual compliance report (March 2025); the Chronicle (Aug 3, 2026) says it is expected to begin in the fall.
properties.notes: Approximate polygon for a real, D4D-adopted block (final D4D, Feb 26, 2020: Table 3.1.1 and Figure 6.2.3) -- see the accuracy note for this shape. Status 'planned': not started as of March 2025, and the Chronicle (Aug 3, 2026) expects construction to begin in the fall. Use 'residential': Table 3.1.1 permits residential, and the design review approved a 339-unit residential building.
